text:
Mr. Perry E. Liller Technical Secretary Stream Pollution Control Board 1330 West Michigan Streat Indianapolis, Indiana 46206
Dear Mr. Miller:
I am the Project Director of an Indiana Criminal Justice Planning Agency grant awarded for the purpose of eradicating wild-growing marihuana within Pulaski County, Indiana. In recent months I have been working on this project with the assistance of other local authorities investigating the best method for eradication of the marihuana.
Recently I was shown a copy of your letter directed to the Chairman of the Board of County Commissioners with copies to the County Health Department and the County Conservation Officer, recommending that aerial spraying of herbicides for the control of weeds and brush along county drainage ditches is not satisfactory because of the adverse effects on the environment, and this method ought to be discontinued.
I have been dealing directly with John L. Clarke, Jr. of Clarke Outdoor Spraying Company, Inc., LaGrange, Illinois, who employs the use of helicopter aerial spraying for marihauana control programs. Mr. Clarke's program includes the use of 2-4D granulated spray applied from the air. A good deal of our problem areas lie along ditch banks.
We wish to do anything and everything necessary to accomplish this project efficiently and without adverse effect on the environment. I am hopeful that we can accomplish this objective with the advice and consent of your department. Following receipt of this letter, a copy of which has been sent to Mr. Clarke, I have asked Mr. Clarke to contact your department to explain his program and answer any questions necessary regarding the spray, its use, and its effects, so that this method can be employed without objection from the stream pollution control board.
